claims.text: A: CISA, through this Directive, provides unified and comprehensive guidance on vulnerability triage by establishing clear remediation timelines. This Directive accounts for many aspects commonly used by vulnerability scoring systems. For example, CVSS contains related information about vulnerable system impact (similar to Technical Impact ), the threat metric is related to whether a vulnerability is in the KEV, and “ Automatable ” is a CVSS version 4 supplemental metric. However, CVSS scores such as “critical” or “high” do not prescribe specific actions. To eliminate ambiguity, CISA replaces these labels with explicit timelines for required remediation under defined conditions. This approach aligns with CVSS guidance that system owners should use threat and environmental information to prioritize vulnerabilities for action. 2 Table 1: Remediation Timelines specifies CISA’s expectations for prioritization using technical, environmental, and threat information. CISA uses vulnerability metadata, which helps define relevant time frames for vulnerability remediation and used reliably at scale.

claims.text: So that you can distinguish Cyber Hygiene scans from random internet noise, we share a link to our source IPs in the Methodology section of your Cyber Hygiene reports and upon request at vulnerability@cisa.dhs.gov. This allows you to properly triage and respond to alerts generated by your security information and event management (SIEM) application. To reduce alerts and conserve analyst resources, it may be prudent to configure your SIEM sensors to avoid generating alerts on traffic from our published addresses. These addresses may change without prior notice, so we recommend regular monitoring.

claims.text: A: CISA’s Cyber Hygiene services can support initial identification of publicly exposed assets by conducting Nmap scans on assets provided by agencies. These Nmap scans will identify some form of active/open/listening port and are therefore considered internet-exposed/public. If no active/open/listening ports are found, the asset could be unavailable or not public/internet-exposed. Our Cyber Hygiene methodology details the re-scan cadence for all asset scopes. After initial identification of publicly exposed assets, you may refer to the Continuous Diagnostics and Mitigation (CDM) Program Agency and Federal Dashboard or review the weekly report’s Attachment section for the most recently attested list of all IPs currently in your agency’s scan scope.
